title: Oswald's Fair Play for Cuba leaflets carry Banister's Camp Street address

tellings.quote: the Fair Play for Cuba leaflets that Lee Harvey Oswald was passing out had the address of Camp Street, the same address.

plain: In New Orleans in 1963, according to the author and researcher Peter Levenda, the leaflets that Lee Harvey Oswald, the man accused of killing President Kennedy that year, handed out for Fair Play for Cuba, a group that supported Fidel Castro's Cuba, were stamped with an address on Camp Street. Levenda says it was the same address, 544 Camp Street, used by a man named Guy Banister, and he tells it as a fact from his own research without naming a source. The point is that it would tie Oswald to Banister's circle rather than leaving him a lone pro-Cuba activist.
